question.problem: Express $\sqrt{\frac{5}{a+b}}\,$ without radicals in the denominator.
question.worked_solution:
First, we apply the quotient rule and put the numerator and denominator under separate radicals:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{5}{a+b}} & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{a+b}}\end{aligned}
$$

To remove the radical $\sqrt{a+b}$ from the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{a+b}$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{a+b}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{a+b}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{a+b}}{\sqrt{a+b}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{a+b}}{\sqrt{a+b}\cdot \sqrt{a+b}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{5(a+b)}}{(\sqrt{a+b})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{5(a+b)}}{a+b} & \end{aligned}
$$
